title: Inquest ordered into Melvin Bigsky shooting
article: --- SASKATOON -- An inquest has been ordered into the death of Melvin Wayne Bigsky, who was shot to death by an RCMP officer during a confrontation on a gravel road near Saskatoon last year.

Bigsky and his wife Rose Ann were passengers in a truck driven by Ivan Indian when a lone RCMP officer attempted to pull them over about eight kilometres east of Saskatoon on the evening of April 27, 2001.
The truck continued travelling down Highway 41 as the cruiser followed with its emergency lights on before turning off on a gravel road for about a kilometre and coming to an abrupt stop.

As the officer waited for backup a chaotic situation developed. The officer struggled with Bigsky when he attempted to take him into custody. Bigsky was pepper-sprayed and struck with a baton and the officer was punched several times during the melee. Bigsky got back into the truck and rammed the police cruiser before he was fatally shot.

The shooting was investigated by the major crimes unit of the RCMP. After reviewing the investigation report, Saskatchewan Justice decided there is no basis for criminal charges and ordered an inquest on Monday.
Divergent accounts of the incident are recorded in documents filed in a civil suit launched by Bigsky's widow.
In her statement of claim, Bigsky alleges that her husband was holding his hands outside the truck window and shouting, "I give up," when he was shot.
In its statement of defence, the RCMP said the constable used his firearm as a last resort to control Bigsky and protect himself and the other occupants of the truck.
No date has been set for the inquest, which will be held in Saskatoon.
